turns.a: The styling. No fill, no visual weight. Label too small to register. Doesn't look like a button you can use. Looks like something turned off.

turns.q: When you look at that greyed-out button, what specific visual cues make it appear "turned off" rather than just inactive?
turns.a: Buttons signal availability through contrast and size. High contrast fill with a readable label. Low contrast, small label. Those are established UI conventions. 'Place Order' has the disabled treatment. Users don't execute buttons that look unavailable. They skip them.

turns.q: What specific visual difference between that greyed-out button and the dark button above it makes you perceive one as available and the other as unavailable?
turns.a: Solid fill: brand color, white label text — standard primary button. WCAG AA: 4.5:1 contrast ratio minimum for the 14–16px label. 3:1 minimum for the button boundary against background. Current gray on gray fails both. One CSS change: background-color, color, font-size. Three properties. Done.
